To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the choline methylation pathway of lecithinsynthesis in the fetal lung is sensitive to acidosis and is restored to normal by alkali infusion.
the rate of choline pathway lecithin formation is reduced by 50% at a pH of 7.0 compared to 7.5, and that this reduction is due to a pH effect on the enzymes of lecithinsynthesis.

acidosis impairs lecithin production in fetal lung slices, that the effect is mediated by the lecithin synthetic enzymes, and that the clinical correction of respiratory acidosis by alkalinization of the blood can be expected to increase pulmonary lecithins to the level found in the normal fetus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biochemical mechanisms responsible for the respiratory distress syndrome of newborn infants, a condition in which the lung fails to function adequately as a gas exchange surface.
the biochemical mechanisms of lung lecithine biosynthesis.
the biochemical and clinical implications of diminished pulmonary lecithinsynthesis in acidosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fetal lung slices incubated at pH 7,0 have a significantly reduced rate of choline incorporation into lecithin compared to slices incubated at a more physiologic pH.

acidosis impairs pulmonary lecithinsynthesis in vitro, that the effect is mediated by the pathway enzymes, and that the biochemical basis for this impairment may account for the pathophysiology of the respiratory distress syndrome.
the rate of lecithine synthesis is reduced at low pH values, and that the rate is restored toward normal with alkali infusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the choline phosphotransferase is the most likely enzyme to be involved in pH-dependent regulation of lung lecithinsynthesis in vivo, although the possibility of a pH-dependent regulatory effect at the level of choline kinase or CDP-choline:1,2-diacylglycerol-cholinephosphotransferase has not been eliminated.
acidosis impairs pulmonary lecithinsynthesis in the fetal lung by reducing the rate of choline incorporation into lecithin.
acidosis is a factor that can contribute to the pathogenesis of the respiratory distress syndrome by interfering with lecithin production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the respiratory distress syndrome is a metabolic acidosis and the correction of acidosis is essential to improve pulmonary lecithins synthesis and improve the respiratory distress syndrome.
acidosis impairs the production of surfactant and this may be one of the reasons for respiratory distress in newborns.
the respiratory distress syndrome is a disease of impaired pulmonary lecithinsynthesis.
